data.title: bn-1rg: Classify unclassified wrapper spawn failures
data.description: For bn-1rg: On synchronized base ba3b75fe41943d2ebfae501c6b5441ac4dbb43ca, classify all failed subprocess spawns as ToolUnavailable while preserving typed native/wrapper exits; add deterministic WouldBlock coverage. Baseline exact focused test passed 25/25, while baseline just check observed NativeFailure in a parallel wrapper invocation test. Post-change exact focused test passed 25/25; deterministic injected-spawn and both affected invocation tests passed; full just check passed on HEAD 469d904. No actual OS ErrorKind was captured for the baseline failure, so the injected WouldBlock case establishes and fixes the source classification path but not the original kernel errno. No timeout, pipe bound, process-group cleanup, or transport classification changed.

data.body: [medium] The generated executable fixture still races parallel process creation. At exact HEAD 469d9045e3576edb7ef854e6266f6697e9193f93, two concurrent teapot_invocation harnesses with --test-threads=32 produced an uninstrumented wrapper-only failure (ToolUnavailable with wrapper_exit=None where Some(0) is required). A forwarding posix_spawn observer then measured ETXTBSY (errno 26) on the generated operator wrapper in both original tests, plus accounting tests. See /tmp/bn-1rg-errno-3shcmfgk/run-06.json and run-20.json. The classification now correctly reports a launch refusal, but the expected wrapper never runs and bn-1rg still fails under parallel stress. The shared helper writes the same inode it later executes, consistent with another spawn temporarily inheriting the writable fd before close-on-exec. Make the fixture execute an immutable launcher and defer per-test script contents to a data file, or otherwise prevent executable write FDs from being inherited. Retain the strict diagnostic and argv assertions and repeat the parallel suite. The prior historical run did not record its errno.

data.reason: Parallel stress reproduced both target fixture failures and a forwarding posix_spawn observer recorded ETXTBSY for each. The production classification change is sound, and bn-1rg remains reproducible until the executable fixture write race is fixed. See th-3j9exz.

data.body: Confirmed ETXTBSY (errno 26) on generated wrapper executables during parallel --test-threads=32 runs. Fixed on HEAD 72b6bd5: test helpers now symlink their bound executable paths to the checked-in, executable test-script-launcher.sh; per-test shell bodies are non-executable data files opened by /bin/sh through HOME. Applied this to teapot_invocation bound_wrapper and playpen_probe, verifier_gate Fixture, and the workspace_process adapter plus its PATH aliases. Added deterministic ExecutableFileBusy and WouldBlock spawn classification coverage. Validation: 32 paired rounds of two concurrent teapot_invocation harnesses at --test-threads=32 (64 harness runs, no failures); focused wrapper/argv tests and all 8 verifier-gate tests passed; full just check passed twice. Review cr-3q7hoc retargeted to this HEAD from base ba3b75f; no vote or close performed.

[medium] The launcher conversion weakens the dispatch sentinel for the earlier nested status controls. The local run() helper sets HOME to its cwd (nested for those controls), but the launcher needs the data file at the outer fixture directory. I ran the exact launcher through an equivalent adapter symlink: with the positive-control HOME it exits 0 and writes the sentinel; with nested HOME, it exits 127 with no sentinel. The final four explicit CLI checks already use the fixture HOME, but the earlier controls can miss an attempted adapter invocation that previously wrote the absolute sentinel. Locate the fixture script and marker relative to the invoked adapter pathname or preserve the original fixture home for every nested-case command. Exercise the positive control with the environment used by the nested commands.

Confirmed at HEAD d44d457: the earlier nested controls used HOME=nested while the immutable launcher data file and sentinel were in the outer temp root. Added run_with_home and pass the fixture root for all three nested controls. The direct adapter positive control uses that same HOME, asserts the sentinel is created, then clears it; each nested control now asserts the sentinel stays absent. The focused hostile-config test passed, followed by 32 concurrent harness pairs (64 exact test runs, zero failures); both full just check runs passed. Review base remains ba3b75f; no vote or close.

Updated result at HEAD d44d457 on base ba3b75f: ETXTBSY errno 26 is covered by the immutable launcher conversion, and the subsequent HOME/sentinel coverage regression is fixed with run_with_home and explicit negative witness assertions. The old review thread remains addressed; 32 pairs of two --test-threads=32 teapot_invocation harnesses passed (64 runs, zero failures), as did focused wrapper/argv tests, all verifier-gate tests, and two full just check runs. No vote or close.

data.reason: The checked-in executable is immutable during fixture setup, and per-test shell bodies are data opened by /bin/sh. Both strict assertions remain. Independent 72b6bd5 stress passed 32 normal and 32 spawn-observed parallel invocation harnesses with no ETXTBSY, and d44d457 changes only the workspace test witness. The final full gate and manifest-pinned Playpen probe test passed.

At d44d457 the three nested controls share the marker-capable HOME with the positive control and each asserts sentinel absence. I independently verified the adapter and both aliases can write the marker from the nested working directory, and the exact workspace case passed 32 parallel harness runs and the final full gate.

Verified full persisted range at d44d4571c8f21d49eafc4b9dd64206b4c45048a2. Both review findings are resolved. Independent focused, parallel, pinned verifier-gate, full just check, and diff checks passed. The earlier live reproduction measured ETXTBSY; the original historical errno is unknown.
